notes: The fixed C1 Held Lines list omits the clocked storage of address portions in ctrl.tag and ctrl.idx at line 126, although lines 180, 181, 225 and 227 show those portions are retained and reused.
Bus-request and bus-response record fields are included only as required entry or exit structural rows and are not treated as primaries because the structural rules bar those fields from qualifying.

points.reason: The process reads the request address and direction and uses them to form cache and backing-bus targets, so changing either redirects or changes the access.
The clocked controller stores address portions in ctrl.idx and ctrl.tag, so corrupting this state changes later cache-line and backing-bus addresses.
The address enters the cache-memory instance and selects tag, valid and data entries, so altering it selects an unintended cache location.
Address-region, atomic and debug tests set buf_dir, and buf_dir selects the direct-bus path instead of the cached path.
The routing decision is retained in ctrl.buf_dir, so overwriting it changes or blocks the selected cache-versus-bypass behavior.
This point only applies a downstream write-enable consequence of the routing decision; it does not store or modify the bypass decision itself.
The instance computes hit_o from valid and tag state, so false hit results alter returned data and timing and can force or avoid backing-bus activity.
The hit result selects immediate acknowledgement and cached data versus a backing-bus transaction, making it observable through response timing and able to alter or stall operation.
The process retains a fence request, enters S_CLEAR, clears the cache and optionally emits a backing-bus fence.
The fence request is held in ctrl.buf_sync, so changing or clearing that register suppresses or fabricates servicing of the fence.
The instance applies the clear command but does not store or compute the fence command itself.
The process uses the host byte-enable field to form cache_o.we, which determines which byte lanes are written.
The write-enable vector controls the individual byte-memory writes, so changing it modifies unintended bytes or omits intended updates.
The controller emits cmd_new during a refill request, and suppressing or fabricating that command changes whether downloaded data is committed as a new cache line.
The new-line command sets valid state and the stored tag, so changing it can validate incomplete data or prevent refill completion.
The process accumulates bus_rsp_i.err, uses it to invalidate a failed fill and reports it as a host error response.
The accumulated error status is retained in ctrl.buf_err, so overwriting or clearing it changes whether a refill is accepted or reported as failed.
The cache-memory instance receives an invalidation consequence of the error status but does not store or compute the status itself.
